name: mtoc
why: Converts Mach-O binaries to PE/COFF, a fascinating look at how executable formats differ and translate.

brief.what_it_is: mtoc is a command-line tool, described in its Homebrew formula as a Mach-O to PE/COFF binary converter, which takes a Mach-O executable (the macOS binary format) and produces a PE/COFF file (the Windows binary format). I could not confirm this from the project's own pages. The Apple Open Source homepage and releases page loaded but never mention mtoc, and the releases page is a dynamic listing that showed no matches. The only source for this description is the formula metadata.
brief.why_it_exists: Not stated in anything I could read. The homepage is a general Apple Open Source portal and says only that Apple releases open source code for its platforms and developer tools.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the Homebrew formula metadata, which lists the executable as 'mtoc' and has no caveats. I saw no README, build instructions, or configuration steps.
brief.standout: The scout note calls it a look at how executable formats differ and translate. That is the editorial angle of whoever submitted it, not something I verified from the project. Apple publishing a Mach-O to PE/COFF converter is unusual, but I could not confirm the tool's details.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage and releases page loaded, but neither mentions mtoc, so I found no last-release date, last commit, or maintenance note.
brief.caveats: I could not reach a project README or documentation for mtoc. Both pages I fetched were Apple's general portal, so the entry should rest on the formula description and should not describe usage, supported platforms, or output quality. The homepage loaded fine; the problem is that it is not a project page for mtoc.
